note.match: Match each person to the banknote they appear on.

rows.label: George Washington
rows.description: Founding Father and first U.S. president (1732–1799)
rows.hook: led the Continental Army and then became the first leader of a new republic

rows.label: Abraham Lincoln
rows.description: president of the United States from 1861 to 1865 (1809-1865)
rows.hook: led the nation through its civil war and issued the Emancipation Proclamation

rows.label: Winston Churchill
rows.hook: led his country through the Second World War with famously defiant speeches

rows.label: Mahatma Gandhi
rows.hook: led a nonviolent independence movement, including the long Salt March

rows.label: Jane Austen
rows.hook: wrote Pride and Prejudice and other sharp romantic comedies of manners

rows.label: Alan Turing
rows.hook: helped crack the Enigma code in wartime and pioneered the idea of the modern computer

rows.label: Alexander Hamilton
rows.hook: was a Founding Father whose life inspired a hit hip-hop stage musical

rows.label: Thomas Jefferson
rows.description: Founding Father, U.S. president from 1801 to 1809 (1743–1826)
rows.hook: wrote the Declaration of Independence and doubled the country's size with a land purchase

rows.label: Nikola Tesla
rows.hook: pioneered alternating-current electricity and was a famous rival of Thomas Edison

rows.label: Isaac Newton
rows.hook: formulated the laws of motion and gravity, famously linked to a falling apple

rows.label: Benjamin Franklin
rows.hook: was a Founding Father and inventor famed for flying a kite in a thunderstorm

rows.label: Ulysses S. Grant
rows.description: president of the United States from 1869 to 1877
rows.hook: commanded the Union armies to victory in the Civil War before entering the White House

rows.label: William McKinley
rows.description: president of the United States from 1897 to 1901 (1843-1901)
rows.hook: led the country through the Spanish-American War and was later assassinated

rows.label: Andrew Jackson
rows.description: president of the United States from 1829 to 1837
rows.hook: became a hero at the Battle of New Orleans before serving as the seventh president

rows.label: Woodrow Wilson
rows.hook: led the country through the First World War and championed the League of Nations

rows.label: Tutankhamun
rows.hook: was a boy king whose treasure-filled tomb with a golden mask was found in the Valley of the Kings

rows.label: Grover Cleveland
rows.hook: is the only president to serve two separate, non-consecutive terms

rows.label: James Joyce
rows.hook: wrote Ulysses, a landmark novel following a single day in Dublin

rows.label: Greta Garbo
rows.hook: was a mysterious film star of the silent era who famously wanted to be alone

rows.label: Hans Christian Andersen
rows.hook: wrote fairy tales such as The Little Mermaid and The Ugly Duckling

rows.label: Gabriel García Márquez
rows.hook: wrote One Hundred Years of Solitude and won the Nobel Prize in Literature

rows.label: Ingmar Bergman
rows.hook: directed The Seventh Seal, with its famous chess game against Death

rows.label: Niels Bohr
rows.hook: developed a model of the atom with electrons orbiting in shells and won a Nobel Prize

rows.label: Diego Rivera
rows.hook: painted enormous public murals and was married to the painter Frida Kahlo

rows.label: William Butler Yeats
rows.hook: wrote The Second Coming and won the Nobel Prize in Literature

rows.label: Claude Debussy
rows.hook: composed Clair de Lune and the orchestral seascape La Mer

rows.label: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
rows.hook: wrote The Little Prince and worked as a pioneering airmail pilot

rows.label: Emilio Aguinaldo
rows.description: President of the Philippines from 1899 to 1902

rows.label: Gustave Eiffel
rows.hook: built a towering wrought-iron landmark on the Champ de Mars in Paris

rows.label: Sejong the Great
rows.description: fourth king of Joseon (Korea), creator of Hangul

rows.label: Astrid Lindgren
rows.description: Swedish writer of fiction and screenplays (1907–2002)
